_comment: Wine Bore curation pack, first cut. Draft until Andy cuts it. Every id is a live wine.* primary key, queried not guessed: producer -> wine.producers.id, appellation -> wine.appellations.id, wine -> wine.wines.lwin, grape -> wine.grapes.id. Notes are the shop's opinion and are loaded with status='draft'. Shelves are a private map, never a menu.

shelves.name: Jura
shelves.blurb: Six hundred hectares of cold clay doing things nobody else dares, and half of it still cheaper than village Burgundy.

members.name: Arbois
members.note: The working appellation. Pupillin is the bit that matters and the label barely says so.

members.name: Côtes du Jura
members.note: Catch-all, which means the grower matters more here than the name does.

members.name: Château-Chalon
members.note: Vin jaune only, six years and three months under the veil, and no way to fudge it.

members.name: L'Etoile
members.note: Tiny, white, chalky. Under-bought because nobody can pronounce it with confidence.

members.name: Maison Pierre Overnoy
members.note: The house everyone copies. Nothing added, nothing removed, and it still outlives the imitators.

members.name: Anne et Jean-Francois Ganevat
members.note: Sixty-odd cuvées and a genius rate of about eighty percent. Buy the Savagnin, skip the wilder end.

members.name: Benedicte & Stephane Tissot
members.note: The range you can actually find. Biodynamic, precise, and the Vin Jaune is a bargain nobody clocked.

members.name: Jean Macle
members.note: Four wines. Château-Chalon done as the rule intends and nothing else attempted.

members.name: Jacques Puffeney
members.note: Retired, so it's a library buy now. The Trousseau was the best argument the grape ever had.

members.name: Domaine Labet
members.note: Single-parcel Chardonnay from limestone. Burgundy prices from the eighties, roughly.

members.name: Bornard
members.note: Ploussard with the brakes off. Volatile in both senses; when it lands it's the best in the region.

members.name: Domaine Pignier
members.note: Old Carthusian cellar, straight winemaking. The one to start a sceptic on.

members.name: Domaine Berthet-Bondet
members.note: Château-Chalon without the collector tax.

members.name: Jean Bourdy
members.note: Fifteen generations. They release old vintages because they can, not as a gimmick.

members.name: Savagnin
members.note: Traminer under another name. Give it air and six years and it does something Chardonnay cannot.

members.name: Poulsard
members.note: Pale enough that people send it back. Their loss.

members.name: Trousseau
members.note: The serious Jura red. Needs a warm slope, gets one rarely.

members.name: Maison Pierre Overnoy, Poulsard, Arbois Pupillin
members.note: The bottle that started the whole natural argument, and it was never about the argument.

members.name: Jean Macle, Chateau-Chalon
members.note: Vin jaune as a reference point. Open it, forget it for a week, it improves.

edges.note: Same oxidative instinct, lid on: Chenin ages without the veil.
Flor taken to its logical end, and with centuries more practice.
The same people drink both; one of them still costs sensible money.
Overnoy's method exported to granite and heat, with less rulebook.

shelves.name: Beaujolais crus
shelves.blurb: Ten named hills that spent forty years paying for what Nouveau did to the region's name.

members.name: Morgon
members.note: Côte du Py is the one you want; the rest of Morgon trades on it.

members.name: Fleurie
members.note: Named for perfume and mostly delivers, which is rarer than it sounds.

members.name: Moulin-à-Vent
members.note: Manganese soils, tannin, ten years in the bottle. The cru that embarrasses Côte de Beaune.

members.name: Côte de Brouilly
members.note: Blue volcanic rock on the cone. Not the same wine as Brouilly and priced as if it were.

members.name: Jean Foillard
members.note: Whole bunch, no sulphur to speak of, and still the most polished thing in the region.

members.name: M. et C. Lapierre
members.note: Marcel's cellar, run straight by the children. The Morgon is the benchmark and they know it.

members.name: Coudert
members.note: Clos de la Roilette. Fleurie on the Moulin-à-Vent side of the fence, and it tastes like it.

members.name: Yvon Metras
members.note: Tiny, expensive, occasionally faulty, and worth the gamble twice a decade.

members.name: Domaine de la Grand Cour (Dutraive)
members.note: Fleurie with real flesh. The most consistent of the natural set.

members.name: Jean-Marc Burgaud
members.note: Not fashionable, never faulty. Côte du Py at trade price.

members.name: Louis Claude Desvignes
members.note: Morgon lieux-dits held apart since before anyone cared. Javernières is the cellar's argument.

members.name: Guy Breton
members.note: Le Petit Max. Gamay drunk cold with something fatty, which is the whole point.

members.name: Chateau Thivin
members.note: Côte de Brouilly's oldest estate and the reason the cru still has a reputation.

members.name: Domaine J. Chamonard
members.note: Long macerations, no additions, Morgon that smells of the cellar. Thin on the ground now.

members.name: Gamay
members.note: Banned from Burgundy in 1395 for being too good at ripening. Still being punished for it.

members.name: Jean Foillard, Morgon, Cote du Py
members.note: The bottle that made everyone take the region seriously again. Keep it five years.

members.name: Coudert, Clos de la Roilette, Fleurie
members.note: The horse on the label is there because the Fleurie growers wouldn't have them. Read that as a compliment.

edges.note: Same cellar habits, colder clay, and a grape nobody has heard of.
Where a thin-skinned red on granite is allowed to cost money.
The white half of the same natural-wine address book.

shelves.name: Loire Chenin
shelves.blurb: One grape, tuffeau, and four degrees of sweetness that the label will not reliably tell you about.

members.name: Vouvray
members.note: Sec to moelleux to sparkling under one name, which is why you buy the grower not the appellation.

members.name: Montlouis-sur-Loire
members.note: Vouvray's south-bank twin, sandier, quicker, and about thirty percent less money.

members.name: Savennières
members.note: Schist, dry, austere for a decade. The least forgiving white in France.

members.name: Saumur
members.note: Chenin on chalk. Underpriced because the name says fizz to most people.

members.name: Domaine Huet
members.note: Three vineyards, one grape, sixty years of proof. The reference and not a nostalgic one.

members.name: Domaine de Clos Naudin (Foreau)
members.note: Huet's opposite number in Vouvray, tighter and slower. The Pétillant is the best value in the Loire.

members.name: Francois Chidaine
members.note: Montlouis grower who bought into Vouvray and got told off for blending across the river. He was right.

members.name: Domaine de la Taille Aux Loups
members.note: Blot makes Chenin taste expensive without oak tricks. The sparkling is serious.

members.name: Nicolas Joly
members.note: Insufferable about biodynamics, correct about the vineyard. Decant it hours ahead or don't bother.

members.name: Domaine du Closel
members.note: Savennières without the lecture. Clos du Papillon is the one.

members.name: Domaine Ogereau
members.note: Layon sweet wines that stay drinkable past one glass, which is the hard part.

members.name: Domaine de Belliviere
members.note: Jasnières, the forgotten north edge. Chenin grown where it barely ripens, and better for it.

members.name: Domaine Guiberteau
members.note: Saumur whites on limestone that read as Burgundy to anyone tasting blind.

members.name: Agnes & Rene Mosse
members.note: Anjou, low sulphur, occasionally cloudy, always intended.

members.name: Chenin blanc
members.note: The most versatile white grape there is, and the most often ruined by a sugar decision.

members.name: Domaine Huet, Vouvray, Clos Bourg Sec
members.note: Dry Vouvray from the best parcel. Undrinkable for five years, then it runs for thirty.

members.name: Nicolas Joly, Savennieres Coulee-de-Serrant
members.note: A monopole since 1130 and still argued about. Worth having the argument once.

members.name: Domaine de Clos Naudin (Foreau), Vouvray, Sec
members.note: The quieter reference. Bone dry, and it will outlive the people who bought it.

edges.note: Chenin's patience taken past the point of oxygen control.
The other acid-and-sugar balancing act, done with a rulebook that states the numbers.
If the Pétillant landed, this is the same trick with a hundred and fifty years of money behind it.

shelves.name: Mosel Kabinett
shelves.blurb: Slate, eight percent alcohol, and the only category in wine where lightness is the achievement.

members.name: Mosel
members.note: The register protects one name for the whole river. Everything that matters happens below that line.

members.name: Nahe
members.note: Mosel tension with a degree more ripeness. Consistently the cheapest good Riesling in Germany.

members.name: Rheingau
members.note: Grander, drier, and the one that went chasing Burgundy when it should have stayed itself.

members.name: Egon Muller
members.note: Scharzhofberg. The most expensive Riesling in the world and the argument holds up.

members.name: Joh. Jos. Prum
members.note: Wehlener Sonnenuhr, reductive on release, glorious at twenty. People give up on it too early.

members.name: Willi Schaefer
members.note: Four hectares in Graach. Domprobst Kabinett is the purest thing on this shelf.

members.name: Peter Lauer
members.note: Saar, barrel-numbered cuvées, the Ayler Kupp Fass 6 as a house wine. Absurd value.

members.name: Hofgut Falkenstein
members.note: Old-school Saar, spontaneous, no filtration. The Kabinetts are what the category was for.

members.name: Forstmeister Geltz Zilliken
members.note: Saarburger Rausch. Cold cellar, slow wines, nothing hurried out of the door.

members.name: Selbach-Oster
members.note: The pragmatist of the middle Mosel. Buys well, makes honestly, never overreaches.

members.name: Immich-Batterieberg
members.note: Dry Mosel done properly, from a blasted-out cliff above Enkirch.

members.name: Clemens Busch
members.note: Pündericher Marienburg split by slate colour. Biodynamic, dry, and it tastes like an argument won.

members.name: Weiser-Kunstler
members.note: Trabener Gaispfad. The best new-ish name on the river, and still findable.

members.name: Riesling
members.note: The only white grape that transmits a slope without translating it. Everything else interprets.

members.name: Egon Muller, Scharzhofberger Riesling Kabinett, Mosel
members.note: Eight percent, twenty grams of sugar, and it lasts longer than most first growths.

members.name: Willi Schaefer, Graacher Domprobst Riesling Kabinett, Mosel
members.note: The bottle to hand someone who says they don't like sweet wine. It ends the conversation.

edges.note: The same acid with the sugar taken out and the alcohol put back.
Same grapes, twice the weight, and a grand cru system that means something.
Identical balancing act on tuffeau, and nobody is bidding at auction for it.

shelves.name: Etna
shelves.blurb: An active volcano with contrade instead of climats, and a twenty-year-old fine wine industry on thousand-year-old vines.

members.name: Etna
members.note: DOC since 1968, taken seriously since about 2002. The contrada on the label is the useful part.

members.name: Faro
members.note: Messina's forgotten Nerello. Three producers and a rule that still exists on paper.

members.name: Sicilia
members.note: The island-wide DOC. Useful for bulk, useless as a guide.

members.name: Terre Siciliane
members.note: Where the interesting Etna bottles go when the grower won't follow the disciplinare.

members.name: Benanti
members.note: Started this, quietly, in the eighties. Pietra Marina is the best Carricante made.

members.name: Tenuta delle Terre Nere
members.note: De Grazia mapped the contrade before anyone else bothered. The wines follow the map.

members.name: Passopisciaro
members.note: Franchetti's altitude experiment. Contrada bottlings that read like a geology lecture, in a good way.

members.name: Azienda Agricola Frank Cornelissen
members.note: Belgian, obsessive, started unfiltered and ended precise. The trajectory is the interesting part.

members.name: Girolamo Russo
members.note: A pianist who took over the family plots. San Lorenzo is the one to buy.

members.name: Graci
members.note: Nerello without make-up. The most straightforwardly likeable estate on the north face.

members.name: Azienda Vinicola Calabretta
members.note: Releases at eight years old because that is when it's ready. Nobody else does this.

members.name: Pietradolce
members.note: Pre-phylloxera vines on Rampante, modern cellar. It works.

members.name: I Vigneri (Salvo Foti)
members.note: Alberello, mule-worked terraces, and a refusal to scale. The conscience of the mountain.

members.name: Palmento Costanzo
members.note: Santo Spirito done cleanly. The house to hand a Burgundy drinker first.

members.name: Nerello Mascalese
members.note: Pale, high-acid, tannic. People call it the Nebbiolo of the south; it's closer to old Pinot.

members.name: Nerello Cappuccio
members.note: The blending partner nobody bottles alone, and it's better alone than they admit.

members.name: Carricante
members.note: Salty, tight, malic. The only Italian white that ages like Riesling.

members.name: Tenuta delle Terre Nere, Etna Rosso, Prephylloxera
members.note: Ungrafted vines from the 1870s. The price is silly and the wine justifies about eighty percent of it.

members.name: Azienda Agricola Frank Cornelissen, Magma, Terre Siciliane
members.note: Barbabecchi at a thousand metres. Divisive, expensive, and not a gimmick.

edges.note: Same bush-vine, low-intervention instinct on granite instead of lava.
Where pale tannic reds have had a market for a century.
Thin skins, volcanic rock, no oak. Half the money.

shelves.name: Piedmont beyond Barolo
shelves.blurb: Nebbiolo grown where the tourists don't go, plus the one white grape the region nearly let die.

members.name: Barbaresco
members.note: Barolo's shorter-aged sibling, thirty percent cheaper for no good reason.

members.name: Carema
members.note: Terraced Nebbiolo at seven hundred metres on the Aosta border. Sixteen hectares, total.

members.name: Lessona
members.note: Marine sand, not limestone. Alto Piemonte Nebbiolo tastes like a different grape and isn't.

members.name: Colli Tortonesi
members.note: Timorasso's home. A DOC that existed for decades before anyone found the point of it.

members.name: Produttori del Barbaresco
members.note: A co-op that outperforms most estates. The Riserva crus are the best value in the Langhe.

members.name: Roagna
members.note: Long macerations, old vines, no new oak, releases late. The most uncompromising house in Piedmont.

members.name: Ferrando
members.note: Carema's keeper. Etichetta Nera in a good year is the whole argument for high-altitude Nebbiolo.

members.name: Proprieta Sperino
members.note: De Marchi replanting Lessona from nothing. Patient, and the wines show it.

members.name: Azienda Agricola Antoniolo
members.note: Gattinara's reference, held by three generations of women. Osso San Grato is the cru.

members.name: Nervi Conterno
members.note: Gattinara bought by a Barolo name, which tells you where the smart money looked.

members.name: Le Piane
members.note: Boca resurrected by a Swiss wine merchant. Volcanic porphyry, and it tastes it.

members.name: Vigneti Massa
members.note: Walter Massa saved Timorasso single-handed. Everyone else in Derthona is following him.

members.name: Comm. G.B. Burlotto
members.note: Verduno. Whole-cluster Barolo, and the Pelaverga is the best cheap red in the region.

members.name: Sottimano
members.note: Neive crus held separate, no make-up. Cottà and Pajorè do different things and prove the point.

members.name: Nebbiolo
members.note: Tannin and acid at the same extreme, and it needs a specific fog to get there.

members.name: Timorasso
members.note: Down to a few hectares in the nineties. Ages ten years and smells of petrol, like a Riesling with a different passport.

members.name: Pelaverga
members.note: Pepper and rose petal at twelve and a half percent. Grown on about twenty hectares and that's the whole world supply.

members.name: Roagna, Barbaresco, Paje Crichet
members.note: Old vines, years in cask, no shortcuts offered. The Barbaresco that answers Barolo directly.

members.name: Ferrando, Etichetta Nera, Carema
members.note: The black label only appears in vintages that deserve it. Which is the correct policy.

members.name: Vigneti Massa, Colli Tortonesi, Costa del Vento Vigna Timorasso
members.note: The bottle that made Timorasso a category instead of a footnote.

members.name: Proprieta Sperino, Lessona
members.note: Nebbiolo on sand. Perfumed where the Langhe is structural, and a third of the money.

edges.note: Granite, thin skins, ten-year wines, sensible prices.
The same pale tannic profile with less history and more volcano.
The other tradition built on releasing wine only when it is ready.

shelves.name: Rioja traditionalists
shelves.blurb: American oak, long ageing, and a handful of houses that never took the consultants' phone calls.

members.name: Rioja
members.note: One protected name, three subzones the register doesn't recognise, and a quality ladder based on time in barrel rather than place.

members.name: Navarra
members.note: Next door, same grapes, none of the reputation. Which is the opportunity.

members.name: Ribera del Duero
members.note: Tempranillo at nine hundred metres in French oak. Grander, and it charges for it.

members.name: R. Lopez de Heredia
members.note: Nothing has changed in the cellar since 1877 and nothing needs to. The white is the sleeper.

members.name: La Rioja Alta
members.note: 904 and 890, racked by hand, released at a decade. The most reliable old-school house going.

members.name: CVNE
members.note: Imperial and Viña Real. Big, and still gets the Gran Reservas right.

members.name: Muga
members.note: Egg whites, wooden vats, no filtration. Prado Enea is the traditional one; ignore the modern cuvées.

members.name: Marques de Murrieta
members.note: Castillo Ygay is released when they feel like it, sometimes twenty years on. Correct.

members.name: Remelluri
members.note: Single estate in Rioja Alavesa, which the region barely allows for. Telmo Rodríguez put the vineyard back together.

members.name: Bodegas Riojanas
members.note: Monte Real Gran Reserva at supermarket-adjacent money. Nobody talks about it.

members.name: Federico Paternina
members.note: Faded, and old vintages of Gran Reserva still turn up cheap. Worth the risk on a case.

members.name: Abel Mendoza
members.note: Varietal Riojas made one grape at a time. An education, not a bottle to impress with.

members.name: Olivier Riviere
members.note: A Frenchman farming old parcels nobody wanted. The new traditional, if that isn't a contradiction.

members.name: Tempranillo
members.note: Low acid, early ripening, and completely dependent on altitude to stay interesting.

members.name: Graciano
members.note: The acid and perfume in a traditional blend. Hard to grow, which is why it nearly vanished.

members.name: Garnacha Tinta
members.note: The warmth in the blend and the grape doing the heavy lifting in old-vine Rioja Baja.

members.name: R. Lopez de Heredia, Tondonia Tinto Gran Reserva, Rioja
members.note: Six years in American oak, released after fifteen, and it still tastes like it was made yesterday by someone in 1920.

members.name: R. Lopez de Heredia, Tondonia Blanco Reserva, Rioja
members.note: Viura and Malvasía, six years in barrel. The most underpriced white wine in Europe.

edges.note: The other Spanish tradition where oxygen and time do the work instead of fruit.
Long ageing with a place-based hierarchy underneath it.
Oxidative handling taken past the point Rioja would permit.

shelves.name: Sherry
shelves.blurb: The most undervalued wine on earth, and the only category where the solera outranks the vintage.

members.name: Jerez-Xérès-Sherry
members.note: Albariza chalk, flor, and a fractional blending system the register actually describes in detail.

members.name: Manzanilla de Sanlúcar
members.note: Same wine, damper cellars, thicker flor. Saltier, and a separate protected name for good reason.

members.name: Montilla-Moriles
members.note: Pedro Ximénez country, no fortification needed. Jerez's cheaper conscience.

members.name: Equipo Navazos
members.note: Two men buying single butts other houses were about to blend away. It changed what the category could charge.

members.name: Valdespino
members.note: Still ferments Inocente in butt from a single vineyard. Nobody else bothers.

members.name: Lustau
members.note: The Almacenista range is a tour of the small stockholders. Best entry point there is.

members.name: Gonzalez Byass
members.note: Tio Pepe en Rama once a year is the point; the rest is volume.

members.name: Barbadillo
members.note: Sanlúcar's biggest, and the old Versos and Reliquia bottlings are extraordinary.

members.name: Hidalgo
members.note: La Gitana. The Manzanilla you can buy anywhere and should more often.

members.name: Emilio Hidalgo
members.note: Different family, smaller cellar. La Panesa Fino Especial is the best fino in Jerez.

members.name: Bodegas Tradicion
members.note: Bought up old soleras and sells nothing young. VORS only, and it earns the acronym.

members.name: Rey Fernando de Castilla
members.note: Antique range, no caramel, no sweetening. Honest amontillado at a fair price.

members.name: Delgado Zuleta
members.note: La Goya. The oldest house in Sanlúcar and nobody in Britain stocks it.

members.name: Palomino
members.note: Neutral, low-acid, dull as table wine. Under flor it becomes the most savoury thing in the shop.

members.name: Pedro Ximénez
members.note: Sun-dried to raisins, four hundred grams of sugar, and it still has grip. Pour it over almost nothing.

members.name: Valdespino, Fino Inocente Single Vineyard Sherry
members.note: Macharnudo Alto, butt-fermented, single vineyard. The bottle that proves terroir survives the flor.

members.name: Equipo Navazos, La Bota de Amontillado No 37 Navazos Sherry
members.note: One butt, bottled as found. This is why people started paying attention again.

edges.note: The same veil of yeast, with no solera and no fortification to steady it.
The other Spanish house style where the cellar outranks the vintage, and it comes as red wine.
The other blended trade wine where a house style beats a single year, priced twenty times higher.

shelves.name: Austrian Grüner
shelves.blurb: Dry, peppery, structural white from loess and gneiss, sold at about a third of what the equivalent Burgundy asks.

members.name: Wachau
members.note: Terraced gneiss on the Danube. Steinfeder, Federspiel, Smaragd is a private ripeness scale, not a register term.

members.name: Kamptal
members.note: Loess over rock, Heiligenstein above it. More generous than the Wachau and cheaper.

members.name: Kremstal
members.note: Between the two and overlooked by both. Which is where the value sits.

members.name: Weinviertel
members.note: The volume zone, and the first Austrian DAC. Peppery, cheap, entirely honest.

members.name: Franz Xaver Pichler
members.note: The Wachau's power benchmark. Unendlich is ridiculous and occasionally worth it.

members.name: Willi Brundlmayer
members.note: Kamptal done completely straight. Käferberg Grüner is the house's real statement.

members.name: Weingut Knoll
members.note: The baroque label and the wines both refuse to modernise. Loibenberg Smaragd ages fifteen years.

members.name: Schloss Gobelsburg
members.note: Monastic cellar, Moosbrugger's Tradition bottlings use nineteenth-century methods on purpose.

members.name: Nikolaihof
members.note: Biodynamic since 1971, before anyone had the word. The Vinothek releases at twenty years old.

members.name: Prager
members.note: Achleiten and Klaus. Tighter than Pichler and better in ten years.

members.name: Franz Hirtzberger
members.note: Singerriedel. Ripe, dense, and the only Wachau estate that can carry that much weight.

members.name: Veyder Malberg
members.note: Bought the terraces nobody would farm. Lower alcohol, no Vinea Wachau rules, better wine.

members.name: Rudi Pichler
members.note: Wösendorf. The unrelated Pichler, and on Grüner the more interesting one.

members.name: Ott
members.note: Wagram loess, Grüner with actual weight and no oak. Bernhard Ott's Fass 4 is the everyday bottle.

members.name: Grüner Veltliner
members.note: White pepper and lentil, and it takes loess better than any other grape. Ages far longer than its reputation.

members.name: Riesling
members.note: On Wachau gneiss it goes dry and stony. A different wine from the Mosel with the same name.

members.name: Franz Xaver Pichler, Unendlich Gruner Veltliner, Wachau
members.note: The maximum case for the grape. Fourteen percent and it still tastes like pepper and stone.

members.name: Weingut Knoll, Loibner Ried Loibenberg Gruner Veltliner Smaragd, Wachau
members.note: Loibenberg at full ripeness, in a cellar that never chased fashion. Keep it a decade.

edges.note: Same grapes plus Gewurztraminer, twice the weight, and a grand cru list to argue about.
The same acid with sugar left in, which is the harder trick.
Where a dry white is allowed to smell of the cellar.

shelves.name: Swartland
shelves.blurb: Old bush vines on granite and schist, farmed by people who left Stellenbosch on purpose.

members.name: Swartland
members.note: A Wine of Origin district, not a European PDO, so the rules govern origin and nothing else. That's the point here.

members.name: Paardeberg
members.note: Decomposed granite. Most of the wines worth buying come off this hill.

members.name: Riebeekberg
members.note: Shale and slate on the other side. Tighter wines, and named on more labels every year.

members.name: Coastal Region
members.note: The catch-all above it, which tells you nothing and appears on plenty of good bottles.

members.name: The Sadie Family
members.note: Eben Sadie found the old vineyards and then told everyone where they were. Columella and Palladius are the reference.

members.name: Mullineux
members.note: Schist, granite and iron bottled separately to prove the soil argument. It works.

members.name: A.A. Badenhorst
members.note: Kalmoesfontein. Old cellar, old vines, no equipment bought after 1950 if he can help it.

members.name: Porseleinberg
members.note: Callie Louw farms schist with a horse and bottles one Syrah. The label is letterpressed; the wine is better than that sounds.

members.name: Testalonga
members.note: Craig Hawkins, skin-contact Chenin, no sulphur to speak of. The wildest thing on the shelf.

members.name: David & Nadia
members.note: Single-site Chenin from the Paardeberg. The most precise whites in the district.

members.name: Alheit Vineyards
members.note: Heritage vineyards across the Cape, blended and single. Cartology is the bottle that converted the sceptics.

members.name: Intellego
members.note: Jurgen Gouws, Chenin and Syrah, no oak to hide behind. Cheap for what it is.

members.name: Lammershoek
members.note: The estate where half the Swartland's winemakers learned. Uneven now, good then.

members.name: Swerwer (JC Wickens)
members.note: Old-vine Chenin from leased parcels. The next one to go up in price.

members.name: Chenin blanc
members.note: South Africa has the oldest Chenin vines on earth and spent forty years distilling them into brandy.

members.name: Syrah
members.note: On granite it goes peppery and thin-skinned, nothing like the Barossa version.

members.name: Cinsaut
members.note: Dismissed as Hermitage and planted everywhere. Old-vine Cinsaut is the Cape's best cheap red.

members.name: The Sadie Family, Columella, Swartland
members.note: Syrah-led blend from a dozen old parcels. The first Cape wine to be worth its price abroad.

members.name: Porseleinberg, Swartland
members.note: One vineyard, one grape, concrete and foudre. As direct as wine gets.

edges.note: Chenin's home ground, with three hundred years of rules attached.
The same low-intervention argument, colder and older.
Bush vines on volcanic rock with a century's head start on the fine wine market.

shelves.name: Alsace
shelves.blurb: Fifty-one grand crus, four noble grapes, and a sweetness level the label is under no obligation to declare.

members.name: Alsace
members.note: One regional PDO covering everything, with the grape on the front and the sugar left unstated.

members.name: Alsace grand cru Rangen
members.note: Volcanic, the steepest and southernmost. Smoky Riesling, and the only grand cru nobody disputes.

members.name: Alsace grand cru Schlossberg
members.note: Granite at Kientzheim, the first cru classified in 1975. Riesling and nothing else worth planting.

members.name: Crémant d'Alsace
members.note: France's biggest Crémant by volume, and at grower level it beats supermarket Champagne without trying.

members.name: Trimbach
members.note: Dry when the region went sweet and never apologised. Clos Ste Hune is the best Riesling in France.

members.name: Domaine Zind Humbrecht
members.note: Biodynamic, botrytis-tolerant, and the sugar varies wildly year to year. Read the indice or be surprised.

members.name: Domaine Weinbach
members.note: Clos des Capucins. The Faller women have run it better than most négociants run anything.

members.name: Albert Boxler
members.note: Sommerberg and Brand, tiny volumes, dry and mineral. The connoisseur's Alsace.

members.name: Domaine Ostertag
members.note: Uses barrels, which scandalised the region. Muenchberg Riesling is the vindication.

members.name: Albert Mann
members.note: Furstentum and Schlossberg, consistently. Nothing flashy and nothing wrong.

members.name: Josmeyer
members.note: Dry Pinot Gris and Auxerrois taken seriously. Hengst Riesling ages twenty years.

members.name: Domaine Marcel Deiss
members.note: Blends the grapes and labels the place, which is illegal in spirit and fought for in court. He was right.

members.name: Marc Kreydenweiss
members.note: Kastelberg schist, biodynamic since 1989. Undervalued because Andlau is the wrong end of the road.

members.name: Domaine Christian Binner
members.note: No sulphur, long élevage, some oxidative notes. Alsace for the Jura crowd.

members.name: Riesling
members.note: The grape the grand crus exist for. Everything else is a passenger with good manners.

members.name: Pinot gris
members.note: Fat, low-acid, often half-sweet without saying so. Good growers make it taste like a wine and not a dessert.

members.name: Gewürztraminer
members.note: Lychee and rose and no acid at all. One glass is a pleasure and two is a mistake.

members.name: Trimbach, Riesling Clos St Hune
members.note: Rosacker limestone, released at five years, drinkable at twenty. The best dry Riesling made anywhere.

edges.note: The same grapes farmed dry, with the sugar question settled before bottling.
Riesling on slate, lighter, and with a rulebook that states the ripeness.
If the Crémant did the job, this is where the same method stops compromising.

shelves.name: Champagne growers
shelves.blurb: Récoltant-manipulants who kept their own fruit instead of selling it to the houses, and priced it accordingly.

members.name: Champagne
members.note: One PDO, three hundred-odd villages, and a grand cru list drawn up for grape prices rather than for taste.

members.name: Coteaux champenois
members.note: The still wine. Thin in nine years out of ten and remarkable in the tenth, which is now more often.

members.name: Rosé des Riceys
members.note: Still Pinot rosé from the Aube, a few hectares, made only in ripe years. Almost nobody has tasted it.

members.name: Jacques Selosse
members.note: Anselme Selosse made growers think like Burgundians and the price followed. Oxidative and divisive, still the hinge.

members.name: Egly-Ouriet
members.note: Ambonnay Pinot, long on lees, low dosage. The most complete grower Champagne going.

members.name: Ulysse Collin
members.note: Took the family vines back off Pommery in 2003. Les Pierrières is the best Blanc de Blancs outside the Côte des Blancs.

members.name: Larmandier-Bernier
members.note: Vertus, biodynamic, almost no dosage. Terre de Vertus is the argument for zero sugar.

members.name: Agrapart & Fils
members.note: Avize, cask-fermented, chalk you can taste. Minéral and Vénus are the ones.

members.name: Jerome Prevost
members.note: Two hectares of Meunier at Gueux, one wine. La Closerie made a dismissed grape respectable.

members.name: Chartogne-Taillet
members.note: Merfy, north of the Montagne. Parcel bottlings from soils nobody had mapped.

members.name: Bereche et Fils
members.note: Ludes. Still one of the few grower names that hasn't gone silly on price.

members.name: Pierre Peters
members.note: Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, and the Réserve Oubliée perpetual blend is the value bottle of the whole region.

members.name: Vouette et Sorbee
members.note: Buxières in the Aube, biodynamic, Kimmeridgian marl. Closer to Chablis than to Reims.

members.name: Chardonnay
members.note: On Champagne chalk it does something it does nowhere else, which is to taste of the rock and not the fruit.

members.name: Pinot noir
members.note: The body in the blend. In Ambonnay and Aÿ it can carry a wine on its own.

members.name: Pinot meunier
members.note: Written off as filler for a century. Prévost and a few others have ended that argument.

members.name: Jacques Selosse, Substance Blanc de Blancs Grand Cru
members.note: A solera of Avize Chardonnay going back to 1986. The most Sherry-like Champagne made, and meant to be.

edges.note: Traditional-method Chenin at a third of the money, and in a good year it holds up.
Where Selosse's oxidative habit came from and where it goes furthest.
The older blended trade wine, solera instead of reserve, and a fraction of the price.
